title: sse: fix chunking/framing for partial JSON + delimiter ordering (streaming stability)
author: Ethan Park
body:
Motivation: We observed multiple customer incidents (ENG-4231) where SSE streaming responses occasionally produced malformed/partial JSON payloads for function/tool-calling and structured-output use cases. Root causes were a) incorrect chunk boundary handling when a JSON token crossed an internal buffer boundary, b) delimiter/event ordering assumptions in the OpenAI-compatibility layer, and c) race conditions between token emission and partial flush leading to out-of-order events. This PR fixes chunking/framing logic to guarantee token-level atomicity for JSON tokens, normalize delimiter emission order, and add deterministic ordering guarantees for data/metadata events in the SSE stream.

Summary of changes: - Introduce a lightweight token-accumulator that tracks incomplete JSON tokens across buffer boundaries and only emits SSE data events when a token is complete. This prevents partial JSON fragments from being sent. - Rework delimiter ordering: we now always emit metadata delimiters ("event: meta" / delimiter markers) before data events when they logically precede them, and we ensure terminal event ordering (e.g., "event: done" follows the final data chunk). - Add defensive parsing and sanity checks in the OpenAI-compatibility layer to detect split multibyte/utf-8 boundaries and coalesce them before UTF-8 decoding. - Add deterministic sequence numbers to SSE comments for easier tracing in logs (no behavioral change to clients). - Add comprehensive unit + integration tests that simulate chunk boundaries at arbitrary offsets and a small harness that fuzzes multibyte boundaries and token splits. - Update streaming README and compatibility notes to document the ordering guarantees and the mitigations for split tokens.

Checklist: - [x] Reproduced incident locally with harness (ENG-4231) - [x] Added unit tests covering split-token and delimiter-order cases - [x] Integration test against OpenAI-compat layer mapping - [x] Benchmarked (minimal overhead; ~0.4% avg token latency increase in microbench) - [x] Security review: no new network surface - [x] Added release notes entry

Compatibility notes: This change is backward-compatible for clients: SSE framing semantics are stricter (fewer partial fragments), and ordering guarantees are stronger which should only help clients. OpenAI-compat behavior preserved, but clients that relied on receiving partial JSON fragments (unsupported) will see fewer partials.

Implementation notes: The accumulator is implemented as a small state machine in sse/streamer.go and is intentionally conservative: it coalesces up to 8KB or until a token-complete boundary is observed. We avoided large allocations by reusing buffers and only copying when crossing a token boundary. The compatibility mapping layer (openai/compat_stream.go) now defers emitting "data: " lines until the streamer confirms token completeness.

Telemetry & observability: Added two new counters: sse.incomplete_token_drops (should be zero after fix) and sse.token_coalesces. Added a debug-only histogram for coalesced_chunk_size. CI: there was a flaky test initially on macOS, I adjusted timeouts for the integration harness.

Notes on testing: The integration harness includes deterministic fixtures (fixtures/sse/chunk-boundary-*.json) and a fuzz runner (tools/sse-fuzz) used in CI for this PR. See commits for details.
commits: fix(sse): accumulator to coalesce partial tokens across buffers
fix(sse): normalize delimiter/event ordering in openai compatibility layer
test(sse): add chunk-boundary unit tests and integration fixtures
docs(streaming): document ordering guarantees and compatibility notes
ci: increase integration harness timeout on macOS CI job
files_changed: sse/streamer.go -- implement token accumulator + coalescing (new state machine)
openai/compat_stream.go -- defer data emission until token completeness confirmed
sse/streamer_test.go -- new unit tests for split-token scenarios
tools/sse-fuzz/main.go -- small harness to fuzz multibyte boundaries
ci/integration.yml -- increased timeout for sse integration job
review_comments: Sofia Patel: LGTM overall, can you add a short note in the streaming README about the new sequence numbers?
Ethan Park (author): Added README note and tests that assert sequence monotonicity.
Lucas Meyer: The accumulator looks good; any perf impact in high-throughput paths? Please add microbench results.
Ethan Park (author): Microbench added to commits, ~0.4% token latency increase on average; numbers included in commit message.
Ava Chen: CI flaky on macOS reproducible in my run; increasing the harness timeout seems fine. Approving after timeout bump.
Sofia Patel: Approved. Verified integration fixture reproduces prior failure and now passes.
release_notes: Fix SSE streaming partial JSON and delimiter ordering: prevents partial JSON fragments in streams and strengthens event ordering guarantees. Improves streaming stability for structured-output and function/tool-calling scenarios.
additional_context: Related incidents: ENG-4231 triggered by a customer using tool-calling with large structured outputs. Follow-up work: consider exposing a client-side retry hint header (ENG-4302).
